published_hypotheses: u is defined as m(12C)/12, carbon-12 unbound, at rest, in its ground state (CIAAW/CODATA definition; restated in the table's name 'atomic mass constant', definition NAMED-NOT-READ in the RMP text).
CODATA 2018 is a least-squares adjustment over data available to 31 December 2018 (closure date NAMED-NOT-READ here); its stated standard uncertainty is 0.000 000 000 50e-27 kg.

A standard atomic weight applies to 'normal materials' (terrestrial); notes g (geological/biological materials outside the limits are known), m (modified compositions in commercial material), r (range of normal material prevents a more precise value) qualify each element (periodictable mass.py header, transcribing CIAAW).
Interval elements (H, Li, C, N, O, Mg, Si, S, Cl) carry an interval; the single figures above are the abridged/conventional values, not the value of any particular sample.

SCOPE OUTSIDE THIS OWNER (noted, not graded): stock.cosmic() (stock.py:243) applies these terrestrial standard atomic weights to Asplund 2009 solar photospheric abundances, a material the CIAAW 'normal terrestrial material' scope does not cover.

MIXED CONVERSION: massform.mu_min_mev (massform.py:2073-2086) adds AME2020 mass excesses in keV to A*U_MEV with U_MEV = U_KG/MEV_KG. lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested for this result. CODATA 2018 did lack data that later moved its value beyond its own stated uncertainty: the 2022 adjustment moves m_u by +1.397e-9 relative, 4.64 sigma of the 2018 uncertainty, and the two tables alone show the move is carried by alpha (alpha shifted -4.55 sigma_2018; -2 dln alpha = +1.370e-9 of the +1.397e-9). Which measurements drove the alpha change is NAMED-NOT-READ here. So, as evidence FOR M's hypothesis in general: a 2018 'recommended value' was incomplete at the 4-5 sigma level. As evidence on THIS tree's conclusions: the move is 1e-9 relative, and the booleans resting on u sit at margins of order 1e-1 (largest central reading 0.309 against 0.5; pair floor 1.997 against 1.9 Mc^2; extra leptons 1.9e28 against 0). Having the 2022 data changes no conclusion. For the atomic weights, the tree's values already equal the current CIAAW 2021 figures; the larger effect is not a lacked datum but the tree's own named approximation H-A (+0.1% in N_n), which also moves no conclusion. Evidence either way is computed in rederive/codata-2018-u.py.
grade_evidence: The value the tree uses is CODATA 2018's m_u exactly (read at the NIST table as transcribed in scipy txt2018, line 1188); the atomic weights equal CIAAW 2021 at the abridged figure (max |rel diff| 1.0e-5 on the payload elements); the tree's named H-A holds for all 14 payload elements over the full CIAAW isotopic intervals (tightest Cl, margin 0.010 nucleon); the tree's data_used (B 4.2109e28, N_e 2.3132e28, N_n 1.8977e28) are reproduced exactly. The one moved datum (u, CODATA 2022, +1.4e-9 = 4.6 sigma_2018) and every other substitution tried (current weights, interval extremes, exact mean nucleon numbers, all combined) leave every boolean resting on the counts (D28's floor, S10's C2 reading, S11/S12's extra leptons, the H-A selftest) unchanged. Hypothesis drifts found (uncertainty dropped, weight intervals and 'normal material' scope dropped, no attribution at stock.py:206, He rounding, 5-s.f. printing of H-A counts) are recorded as discrepancies and computed to move nothing. Caveat on the reading: the primary papers were not reached (alphaXiv quota exceeded; arxiv.org, NIST and ciaaw.org 403 at the proxy); the values were READ at verbatim machine transcriptions of the published tables, so read_status is READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT and the tree's own NAMED-NOT-READ status is not lifted by this audit.
what_would_change_the_grade: OPEN if the transcriptions (scipy txt2018/txt2022, periodictable mass.py) were shown not to match the NIST/CIAAW primary tables; reading the RMP 93 025010 table and Prohaska 2022 Table 1 directly would upgrade the read to READ. DATA-DEPENDENT only if a conclusion's margin shrank to the 1e-3 level: that would take the C2 reading within ~0.001 of 0.5 or the floor within ~0.001 of 1.9 Mc^2, far from 0.309 and 1.997 now. NARROWED if the payload's isotopic composition were shown to lie outside the CIAAW intervals by more than 0.010 nucleon for chlorine (H-A's tightest margin), e.g. a non-terrestrial or isotopically enriched payload, or if stock.ATOMIC_MASS were applied in this owner to a non-terrestrial composition.
